findings.property: Every executable program input must be included in the reviewed file pins; commands must not execute caller-supplied stdin as script text.
findings.evidence: scripts/task-run-guard.py:175-181 deliberately sets script_index to None when Python argv contains '-', and the Bash branch at 183-186 leaves script_index unset for '-s' because it is an option. The later regular-input scan (199-219) only examines argv entries and cannot inspect stdin. subprocess.Popen at 379 inherits the guard process stdin. Thus policy actions such as ['/usr/bin/python3', '-'] and ['/usr/bin/bash', '-s'] are admitted without a pinned script file and read executable source from inherited stdin; the review/pin checks do not cover those bytes. This contradicts the approved whole-path requirement that executable/script inputs be pinned regular files. I did not run an extra behavioral probe because only the specified affected suite was authorized.
findings.falsifier: Reject stdin-program modes (including Python '-' and Bash '-s') before journal mutation/dispatch, or define and enforce an explicit pinned regular stdin source; add affected tests showing no marker executes from inherited stdin and preserving valid argv literal controls.

findings.falsifier: No later test can establish historical ordering. Only an explicit authorized plan amendment could change this evidence requirement; absent that, this remains unmet and must not be described as tests-first compliance.
